title: Barbershop Etiquette: Arriving, Phones, Payment and Cancelling
hero_alt: Black tufted barber chair inside Divinely Faded, ready for the next appointment
card_text: Book ahead, show up on time, mind the phone, pay after, cancel early: how a visit to my chair works.
lede: Good barbershop etiquette comes down to four things: book ahead, show up on time, keep the phone away from your ears while I'm working there, and cancel early if you can't make it. At my shop, every visit is an appointment through Booksy, and you pay after the cut.
None of it is complicated. Here is how each part works at Divinely Faded.

seo.title: Barbershop Etiquette: Arriving, Paying, Cancelling
seo.description: Barbershop etiquette at Divinely Faded in Carlsbad, NM: booking ahead, arriving on time, phones in the chair, paying after and cancelling early.

subsections.heading: Book first
paragraphs: I cut by appointment only. Booksy shows every open time and is where you choose your service. If nothing fits, text me rather than showing up and hoping.

subsections.heading: Be on time
paragraphs: I work solo, so your appointment is a set piece of my day. Plan for traffic, so the cut starts when it should and nobody is squeezed.

subsections.heading: Pick the right service
paragraphs: The Essential Haircut is the cut alone. If your beard needs a trim or a line-up, the Signature Cut is the booking that has room for it, so choose it from the start.

subsections.heading: Booking for a kid
paragraphs: Kids book on Booksy the same way you do, from the same menu. Put the appointment under the service they need, and come in with them.

subsections.heading: Bring a photo
paragraphs: A screenshot of the cut you want, saved before you arrive, does most of the explaining for you. Have it ready when you sit down.

blocks.heading: Phones and stillness.
blocks.lead: Small things that help the cut.
paragraphs: A phone held up to your ear sits right where the clippers need to go around the ear and neckline. If a call can't wait, say so first, so the work can stop at a safe moment rather than mid-line.

Keep your head where I set it, especially when the straight razor comes out. Glasses come off for the sides and back, so keep them close to check the finished cut. If something feels off, like a towel that's too hot, tell me right away.
Earbuds are fine for music, but they sit right where the edges around the ear get cleaned up, so expect to take them out for that part.

blocks.heading: Pay after, your way.
paragraphs: Payment is due in full once the service is finished, not before. I take cash, card, Zelle and Cash App.
Booking on a holiday? Appointments on the holiday itself carry a {{holiday_fee}} holiday fee on top of the service, so expect it on the bill. The days around the holiday are regular prices.
Want an add-on, like a wash and scalp massage for {{addon:wash-scalp-massage}}? Choose it on Booksy when you book.

blocks.heading: If plans change.
paragraphs: The moment you know you can't make it, cancel or move the appointment in the app. Skipping it, or cancelling at the last minute, may cost you a fee.

Cancelling early also opens the slot for someone else. With one barber, a slot that sits empty is a haircut that doesn't happen. Rescheduling works the same way: move the appointment in Booksy rather than skipping it. Feeling sick counts as plans changing, so move the visit instead of coming in.
Running behind? Text me at {{phone}} so I know you're on the way.

blocks.heading: Say it early.
paragraphs: Tell me up front how much comes off the sides, how long the top stays, and whether the beard is part of it. If the beard needs work, book the Signature Cut rather than the Essential, so the time for it is already on the calendar.
If something looks different from what you pictured, say so while the cut is still going. A change is easy mid-cut and much harder once the sides are already short.
Texting is the quickest way to reach me, before or after the visit. Save {{phone}} in your phone so it's there when you need it.

items.q: Do I need to book ahead for a haircut?
items.a: Yes. Every visit at Divinely Faded is booked in advance on Booksy.
Text me as soon as you know, so I'm not left guessing whether you're coming.

items.q: Can I text instead of calling?
items.a: Yes. I'd rather get a text than a call, and texting is the quickest way to reach me.
After the service. Cash, card, Zelle and Cash App all work.

items.q: Is there a fee for cancelling?
items.a: No-shows and late cancellations may be charged a fee through Booksy. Cancel well ahead and you keep that off the table.
